nodes.summary: Polarized `ABBA` indicator (Durand et al. 2011): `P1` and `O` ancestral, `P2` and `P3` derived.
nodes.title: Polarized ABBA site-pattern indicator

nodes.summary: Unpolarized `ABBA` indicator for populations `(P1, P2, P3, O)`: `P1` agrees with `O`, `P2` with `P3`, and `P1` differs from `P2` (the patterns `ABBA` and `BAAB`).
nodes.title: Unpolarized ABBA site-pattern indicator

nodes.summary: Polarized `BABA` indicator (Durand et al. 2011): `P1` and `P3` derived, `P2` and `O` ancestral.
nodes.title: Polarized BABA site-pattern indicator

nodes.summary: The site-pattern identity: `1[BABA] - 1[ABBA] = (x₁ - x₂) (x₃ - x₄)` for every configuration of derived-allele indicators.
nodes.title: ABBA–BABA site-pattern identity

nodes.summary: Unpolarized `BABA` indicator for populations `(P1, P2, P3, O)`: `P1` agrees with `P3`, `P2` with `O`, and `P1` differs from `P2` (the patterns `BABA` and `ABAB`).
nodes.title: Unpolarized BABA site-pattern indicator

nodes.summary: Probability of the derived/ancestral configuration `x` when haplotype `i` is sampled independently and carries the derived allele with probability `q i`.
nodes.title: Probability of a derived-allele configuration

nodes.summary: The unbiased `f2` estimator of Patterson et al. (2012), Appendix: `(â - b̂)² - â (1 - â) / (m_A - 1) - b̂ (1 - b̂) / (m_B - 1)` with `â = x_A / m_A`, written as `(x_A / m_A - x_B / m_B)² - x_A (m_A - x_A) / (m_A² (m_A - 1)) - …`.
nodes.title: Unbiased f2 estimator

nodes.summary: The unbiased `f3` estimator of Patterson et al. (2012), Appendix: `(ĉ - â) (ĉ - b̂) - ĉ (1 - ĉ) / (m_C - 1)`.
nodes.title: Unbiased f3 estimator

nodes.summary: If the lineage weights of `T` are an affine combination `∑ k, w k • weight (S k)` of those of the sources (`∑ k, w k = 1`, weights of any sign), then `f4 T X Y Z = ∑ k, w k * f4 (S k) X Y Z`.
nodes.title: qpAdm model equation in the drift model

nodes.summary: qpAdm model equation (Haak et al. 2015, Supplementary Information): if the target `T` is an admixture of sources `S k` with weights `w k` summing to `1` (`p T = ∑ k, w k * p (S k)` pointwise; the weights may be negative, as in fitted qpAdm models), then for all `X`, `Y`, `Z`, `f4 T X Y Z = ∑ k, w k * f4 (S k) X Y Z`. The merged `DriftModel.f4_admixture_right` is a two-source drift-model instance (mixture in the…
nodes.title: qpAdm model equation

nodes.summary: Linearity of `f4` in its first pair: if `p A - p B = ∑ l, c l * (p (C l) - p (D l))` pointwise, then `f4 A B Y Z = ∑ l, c l * f4 (C l) (D l) Y Z`.
nodes.title: Linearity of the f4-statistic in its first pair

nodes.summary: The `f4` estimator `(â - b̂) (ĉ - d̂)`; it needs no correction for four distinct populations.
nodes.title: f4 estimator

nodes.summary: The qpWave matrix of left populations `L 0, …, L n` and right populations `R 0, …, R r`: entry `(i, j)` is `f4 (L (i + 1)) (L 0) (R (j + 1)) (R 0)`.
nodes.title: qpWave matrix of f4-statistics

nodes.summary: Unbiased estimator of `p (1 - p)` from `x` derived copies among `m` sampled copies: `x (m - x) / (m (m - 1))` (meaningful for `m ≥ 2`).
nodes.title: Unbiased heterozygosity estimator

nodes.summary: Hudson's `F_ST` denominator estimator `â (1 - b̂) + b̂ (1 - â)` (Bhatia et al. 2013); the numerator estimator is `f2Hat`.
nodes.title: Estimator of Hudson's F_ST denominator

nodes.summary: Hudson's `F_ST` denominator at one site: `p_A (1 - p_B) + p_B (1 - p_A)`, the probability that two copies, one from each population, differ. The numerator is `(p_A - p_B) ^ 2`.
nodes.title: Hudson's F_ST denominator at one site

nodes.summary: Hudson's `F_ST` lies in `[0, 1]` for frequencies in `[0, 1]`. (When the denominator vanishes the junk value `0` also lies in `[0, 1]`, so no positivity hypothesis is needed.)
nodes.title: Hudson's F_ST lies between 0 and 1

nodes.summary: Hudson's `F_ST` over sites `s` in the ratio-of-averages form of Bhatia et al. (2013): `∑ s, (p_A s - p_B s) ^ 2 / ∑ s, hudsonDen (p_A s) (p_B s)`. It is defined when the denominator is positive (it vanishes only if every site is fixed for the same allele in both populations); otherwise Lean's value `0` is a junk value.
nodes.title: Hudson's F_ST (ratio of averages)

nodes.summary: The sample frequency is unbiased: for `X ~ Bin(m, p)` with `m ≥ 1`, `E[X / m] = p`. (For `m = 0`, `X / 0 = 0` is a junk value, hence `m ≥ 1`.)
nodes.title: Sample allele frequency is unbiased

nodes.summary: `sampleExpect` is the expectation under independent sampling: if the derived-allele indicators `X i` are independent random variables with `P(X i = true) = q i`, then `E[g (X 0, …, X (n - 1))] = sampleExpect g q`.
nodes.title: Sampling expectation is an expectation of independent indicators

nodes.summary: Unbiased `f2` (Patterson et al. 2012, Appendix): with independent binomial samples `X_A ~ Bin(m_A, p_A)`, `X_B ~ Bin(m_B, p_B)`, `m_A, m_B ≥ 2`, `E[f2Hat] = (p_A - p_B) ^ 2`, the population `f2` at the site.
nodes.title: Unbiased `f2`

nodes.summary: Unbiased `f3` (Patterson et al. 2012, Appendix): with pairwise independent binomial samples, `m_C ≥ 2` and `m_A, m_B ≥ 1`, `E[f3Hat] = (p_C - p_A) (p_C - p_B)`.
nodes.title: Unbiased `f3`

nodes.summary: For four populations sampled independently across the two pairs (`m ≥ 1` each), `E[f4Hat] = (p_A - p_B) (p_C - p_D)`; no correction is needed.
nodes.title: Unbiased `f4`

nodes.summary: For `X ~ Bin(m, p)` with `m ≥ 2`, `E[X (m - X) / (m (m - 1))] = p (1 - p)`.
nodes.title: Unbiased heterozygosity

nodes.summary: Hudson's denominator is unbiased (Bhatia et al. 2013): with independent binomial samples (`m ≥ 1` each), `E[hudsonDenHat] = hudsonDen p_A p_B`.
nodes.title: Hudson's denominator is unbiased

nodes.summary: In the drift model, if no edge lies on both the `P1–P2` and the `P3–O` path (as on the tree `((P1, P2), P3), O`), then the expected unpolarized `ABBA` and `BABA` counts are equal. Thus `BABA - ABBA` and its sign reversal have expectation `0`. The integrability hypotheses make both expectations meaningful.
nodes.title: The unpolarized D-statistic numerator vanishes on a tree

nodes.summary: When the frequencies `p X ω` are themselves random (drift, and the choice of locus) and one haplotype is sampled from each population independently given the frequencies, the expected `BABA - ABBA` difference is `f4 P1 P2 P3 O`.
nodes.title: ABBA–BABA equals `f4`

nodes.summary: Hudson's `F_ST`, ratio of averages (Bhatia et al. 2013): the ratio of the expected summed numerator and denominator estimators is the population `hudsonFst`. This is a statement about the ratio of expectations; the expectation of the ratio of the estimated sums is in general not `hudsonFst`.
nodes.title: Hudson's `F_ST`, ratio of averages

nodes.summary: Summed over sites, Hudson's numerator estimator `∑ s, f2Hat` is unbiased for `∑ s, (p_A s - p_B s) ^ 2` (independence is needed only within each site).
nodes.title: Unbiasedness of the summed f2 estimator

nodes.summary: Summed over sites, Hudson's denominator estimator is unbiased for `∑ s, hudsonDen (p_A s) (p_B s)`.
nodes.title: Unbiasedness of the summed Hudson denominator estimator

nodes.summary: qpWave rank bound (Reich et al. 2012, Supplementary Information; Patterson et al. 2012): if the frequency of every left population `L i` is an affine combination `∑ l, a i l * p (S l)` (`∑ l, a i l = 1`, coefficients of any sign) of the frequencies of `k + 1` source populations, then the matrix `f4 (L i) (L 0) (R j) (R 0)` (`i, j ≥ 1`) has rank at most `k`; with `k` sources, at most `k - 1`. The right populations…
nodes.title: qpWave rank bound

nodes.summary: `sampleExpect` is additive in the function.
nodes.title: Additivity of the sampling expectation

nodes.summary: Polarized form (Durand et al. 2011, with `q 3` the derived-allele frequency in the outgroup): `E[BABA_pol - ABBA_pol] = (q₁ - q₂) q₃ (1 - q₄)`. When the outgroup is fixed for the ancestral allele (`q 3 = 0`) this is `(q₁ - q₂) (q₃ - q₄)`, as in the unpolarized identity.
nodes.title: Expected polarized ABBA–BABA difference

nodes.summary: ABBA–BABA identity (Patterson et al. 2012; Durand et al. 2011): under independent sampling of one haplotype per population at derived-allele frequencies `q` (any reals; frequencies in `[0, 1]` in the biological model), `E[BABA - ABBA] = (q₁ - q₂) (q₃ - q₄)`.
nodes.title: ABBA–BABA identity

nodes.summary: `sampleExpect` of a product of functions of single coordinates factorizes: `E[∏ i, g i (x i)] = ∏ i, (g i true * q i + g i false * (1 - q i))`.
nodes.title: Sampling expectation of a product factorizes

nodes.summary: `sampleExpect` commutes with subtraction of functions.
nodes.title: Sampling expectation commutes with subtraction

nodes.summary: Expectation of a function `g` of the configuration under independent sampling of one haplotype per population at derived-allele frequencies `q`.
nodes.title: Expectation under independent haplotype sampling

nodes.summary: At each site Hudson's numerator is at most the denominator for frequencies in `[0, 1]`: the difference is `p_A (1 - p_A) + p_B (1 - p_B) ≥ 0`.
nodes.title: Hudson's numerator is at most the denominator

nodes.summary: The configuration probabilities sum to `1`.
nodes.title: Configuration probabilities sum to one

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
